html:
Liberia is a country on the Atlantic coast of West Africa, founded by freed African Americans and independent since 1847. The map shows it from 1880 to the present. With Ethiopia, it was one of only two African states never colonised by Europeans.

It began in 1822 as a settlement of the American Colonization Society, a group of white Americans who wanted to send free Black people to Africa, some out of anti-slavery belief and some to be rid of them. Over the next four decades about 15,000 African American settlers arrived, along with Africans freed from slave ships. The capital, Monrovia, was named after President James Monroe.

The settlers declared independence in 1847 under Joseph Jenkins Roberts. For over a century the Americo-Liberians, a small minority, ruled the many native peoples of the interior through the True Whig Party, much as a colonial elite. The scholar Edward Wilmot Blyden, who settled there, became a founder of Pan-African thought. From 1926 the American Firestone company ran one of the world's largest rubber plantations in Liberia.

In 1980 Samuel Doe, a soldier from a native people, killed President William Tolbert and seized power. Charles Taylor's rebellion in 1989 began two civil wars, which lasted until 2003 and killed a great many people. In 2006 Ellen Johnson Sirleaf became Africa's first elected woman head of state. Liberia was then struck by the Ebola epidemic of 2014 to 2016.
